children: Canada and France plan to cooperate on space-launch systems and ground-based infrastructure as Ottawa seeks closer economic and security ties with Europe.

Prime Minister Mark Carney announced the initiative Sunday with French President Emmanuel Macron in Saint-Pierre and Miquelon, the French territory near Canada’s Atlantic coast. The countries directed their space agencies and defense departments to develop and share infrastructure, though they did not disclose funding or a timetable.

The agreement reflects Canada’s effort to reduce its reliance on the U.S. amid an escalating trade dispute. For investors, closer cooperation could generate opportunities for Canadian and European aerospace, defense, satellite communications and infrastructure companies. However, the absence of budgets or project deadlines means the near-term commercial impact remains uncertain.

Carney said national sovereignty increasingly depends on secure access to strategic technologies and resources, including artificial intelligence, semiconductors, critical minerals, clean energy and space systems.

The announcement follows a European Union proposal to establish Canada as the bloc’s first associate member. Ottawa is seeking a broader relationship with Europe as U.S. tariffs and retaliatory Canadian measures disrupt trade between the neighboring countries.

Canada and France also agreed to expand regional cooperation involving Atlantic Canada and Saint-Pierre and Miquelon. The effort will cover fishing, telecommunications, energy and economic development.

title: Canada, France plan space partnership as Ottawa deepens European ties
